items.title: Header Brands link → Daybird card → filtered catalog → "All brands" back to /brands
covers: AC1: header Brands link opens the Brands page
AC1: cards alphabetical with counts and 'from $x.xx'
AC1: card opens catalog with only that brand's items and header 'Brand: <name>'
AC1: 'All brands' lands on /brands with heading 'Brands' and the Brands nav link current
AC1: filtered catalog shows the card's item count
items.reason: AC1 is the epic's main round trip: BRAND-1's header link and page, BRAND-2's card link, brand header and "All brands" link, in one session. Each story tests its part from a direct URL; only this case proves the hand-offs (the page reached from the header has working card links, the card count matches what the catalog shows, the way back restores the Brands page and nav state). e2e because it is browser navigation across WebApp pages.

items.title: Every brand card's product count equals the item count of the catalog it opens
covers: AC1: the filtered catalog showed exactly that brand's item count from the card
items.reason: AC1's outcome ties two stories' numbers together: BRAND-1's count comes from the new summary endpoint, BRAND-2's filtered catalog from the existing items endpoint. If the two queries count differently (for example a join or filter mismatch in the summary), one brand would show a different number on its card than in its catalog. TC-EPIC-359-01 checks one brand; this case checks all 13 so a mismatch on any brand fails. e2e because the comparison is between what two WebApp pages show.

items.title: Sort by "Most products", reload, then open the top brand's products
covers: AC2: choosing 'Most products' adds ?sort=count and orders by count descending, then by name
AC2: reload keeps the order and the selected option
AC2: first card opens /?brand=<id of top brand> with header 'Brand: <that brand>' and that many items
items.reason: AC2 crosses all three stories: BRAND-3's sort control and URL state must survive a reload, and the cards it reorders must still carry BRAND-2's links to the right brand (a reorder that kept links in name order would open AirStrider from the Gravitator card). The top brand is decided by a tie (three brands at 11), so the case also proves the name tie-break reaches the link. e2e because it involves a browser reload and navigation.

The test asserts aria-current after the reload, but the keyframe for that highlight (08 'After reload: Most products selected') and every other post-reload frame (09-13) show only the card grid, scrolled down with the Sort control above the viewport. The only frame showing 'Most products' selected (03) is from before the reload. Bring the Sort control into view after page.reload() (for example scroll to top or scrollIntoViewIfNeeded) before the highlight, so the recording proves the selection survived the reload.
